title: Small AI Teams with Huge Impact — Vik Paruchuri, Datalab
talk_summary: Vik Paruchuri describes running Datalab (40K GitHub stars, seven-figure ARR, state-of-the-art OCR models) with a team of 3-4 senior generalists, arguing headcount does not equal productivity. The mechanisms are organizational: hire senior generalists, keep tech simple and modular so AI can contribute, minimize process, and use AI to fill low-leverage edges rather than hiring specialists.

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately avoid specialists and handoffs, having one person own a problem end-to-end from customer conversation through training and integration, because each handoff loses context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time you hand off between teams in a traditional company, you lose context

takeaways.technique: Modular, AI-friendly codebase as context substrate
takeaways.what_they_do: They rearchitected their main repo to be extremely modular, well documented, and simple (server-rendered HTML, no React) specifically so AI can add to it reliably.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we rearchitected our marker repo to be extremely modular and easy to to work with and well documented and that makes it much easier to use AI to actually add to it

takeaways.what_they_do: After layoffs they cut low-value features and found that small teams must ruthlessly prioritize because there is always more work than capacity; large teams invent work for themselves.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you have a tiny team, there's so much work that you actually have to ruthlessly prioritize

takeaways.technique: AI for low-leverage edges, humans/strong models for core
takeaways.what_they_do: They used AI specifically on the easy, low-leverage pieces (data pipeline library, API integration) while doing the high-level work themselves in each silo.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we used AI to to take kind of the easy lowleverage pieces of this

takeaways.technique: Simple boring tech, one big machine over clusters
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue against Kubernetes-style complexity for small teams, citing the shell-script-on-one-big-machine pattern over distributed clusters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need a Kubernetes cluster when you're a threeperson company

takeaways.what_they_do: Hiring is a short peer chat, then a ~10-hour paid project ($1,000), then a culture-fit conversation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do a paid project. It's usually around 10 hours. We pay $1,000
takeaways.numbers: ~10 hours, $1,000 per trial; ~40% of interviewed candidates hired
